title: Transient Burst Latency Rebalancer: soft-eviction slot pooling and kernel-preemption hints
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe transient "bursts" of short requests (prefill-heavy or fanout chat starts) that cause the admission controller to either over-serialize (small slots per batch -> higher per-token cost) or over-aggregate (large batches -> tail latency spikes when heavy decodes join). This leads to 99.9th percentile latency regressions for seeded chat workloads and mobile clients.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight runtime component (Burst Latency Rebalancer) that rebalances slot allocation across short-lived bursts by combining: (1) soft-eviction slot pooling to quickly reclaim and reuse warm KV slots for similar prefill shapes, (2) kernel-preemption hints so long-running decode work can yield to latency-sensitive prefill windows, and (3) an amortized admission-cost estimator that accounts for attention-optimization benefits (fusion, merged keys) when deciding batch shaping. The feature should reduce p99 prefill latency by ~25% for bursty traffic while keeping token-cost increase under 5%.

Scope: prototype in the serving runtime admission path + simulator, followed by controlled canary on dedicated pool. Workstreams: admission API changes, slot-pool lifecycle, preemption hint contracts, estimator model training, observability (per-request cost and tail contribution).

Non-goals: overhaul of kernel selection algorithms (we will reuse existing kernel-ranking), broad scheduling rewrite — focus on admission shaping and light-weight preemption signals.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated workloads (burst: 200 req/min with 80% short prefill) show p99 prefill latency reduction >= 20% vs baseline
End-to-end canary on dedicated pool demonstrates p99 improvement >= 15% and token-cost change <= 5%
New metrics ingested to Console: burst_slot_reuse_rate, preemption_yield_count, amortized_admission_cost
Automated correctness tests for slot lifecycle and race conditions included in CI
Operational runbook updated and rollback flag available via runtime-config
design_notes: Soft-eviction slot pooling: maintain a small LRU cache of recently released prefill KV slots keyed by shape fingerprint (seq_len distribution + model variant). Eviction is soft: we prefer reuse but allow preemption if decode work needs the slot.

Kernel-preemption hints: annotate decode RPCs with a reclaimable bit and an estimated remaining tokens number. Kernel scheduler will accept voluntary yield points to commit partial decode state and free GPU temp buffers for short prefill work.

Amortized admission-cost estimator: lightweight linear model that combines per-shape kernel-time profile (from perf cache) and attention-fusion savings estimate to decide whether to admit immediately or delay up to N ms to aggregate larger batch safely.

Trade-offs: small risk of added jitter if estimator mispredicts; mitigated by conservative defaults and short max-delay cap (configurable). Also need to ensure no data leakage across KV slot reuse — enforced by per-customer tenant checks.
Fallback policy: when the pool is exhausted or estimator uncertain, revert to current slot allocation behavior to preserve safety. Canary guardrails will monitor error rates closely.
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement simulator harness to reproduce burst patterns and baseline metrics (Diego)
Week 2: implement slot-pool data structure + API for soft-evict/reuse (Diego + Lena Hoffman), add unit tests
Week 3: add kernel-preemption hint plumbing and voluntary yield hook in decode loop (Diego), validate with microbenchmarks
Week 4: train simple amortized admission-cost estimator from perf-cache data, integrate into admission path (Asha)
Week 5: end-to-end integration, add console metrics and dashboard (observability team), run canary on a subset of dedicated capacity
Week 6: iterate on thresholds from canary, prepare rollout and runbook, cut runtime-1.26 canary release
testing_and_results: Simulator run (2026-03-12): baseline p99=420ms, prototype with soft-pool only p99=320ms (24% improvement), token-cost delta +1.8%
Microbenchmark preemption yield (2026-03-13): average reclaim latency 3.2ms, yield success rate 98% on A100 backends
Canary plan: 100 QPS on dedicated pool for 48h, compare p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics against matched baseline nodes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: slot reuse could leak KV contents between tenants -> mitigation: zeroization and tenant-tag check on reuse, mandatory eviction on cross-tenant mismatch
Risk: estimator misprediction -> mitigation: conservative max_delay_ms=15ms and fallback immediate admission; roll threshold adjustable via runtime-config
Risk: decode preemption could reduce throughput for long-running decodes -> mitigation: only enable hints for models with preemption-friendly kernels; feature gate by model profile
